name: Week 17 Pull — Steady State (Spotlight: Chest-Supported Row + Reverse Fly)
description: Volume steady; the protective behind-back shrug stays front-loaded as activation. The DB row pyramid holds at 70/80/90 bare-hand — grip stays the honest limiter, no straps. Face pull moves to 47.5 with the fist / knuckles-up grip that unlocked it. Cable crunch drops to 62.5 to win back true ab flexion. Spotlights cycle forward to the chest-supported row and the reverse fly — the two upper-back / rear-delt lifts that keep the shoulder healthy, drilled for the glued-chest and slow-eccentric patterns. Cable lifts list a number per equipment option.

dayOverview.theme: Steady state. Shrug stays FIRST (protective activation). DB row pyramid holds 70/80/90, no straps. Face pull 47.5 (fist / knuckles-up grip). Cable crunch 62.5 for true ab flexion. Spotlights cycle to chest-supported row + reverse fly. Cable lifts list per-equipment numbers.

spotlights.why: Cycles forward — the glued-chest, elbow-to-hip pattern is the backbone of healthy rowing. Spotlight drills the chest-stays-down cue and the full stretch-to-squeeze ROM at 40, so the lats do the work and the lower back stays out of it.

Cycles forward — the rear-delt / mid-trap work that balances all the pressing and protects the shoulder. Spotlight drills the fixed soft elbow + lead-with-the-elbow sweep + 2s eccentric at 20, capping reps with tempo rather than chasing the number.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W15 chest-supported row + face pull · W16 lat pulldown + incline curl · W17 chest-supported row + reverse fly (current) · W18 cycle forward — pull-up + DB row refresh.
watchpoints: **Behind-back shrug stays FIRST (activation slot).** Front-loading it keeps pull day flare-free — it's the protective counter-movement to all the pulling and can't be the piece a rushed session drops. Right after the warmup.

**DB row holds 70/80/90, no straps.** The top set is 90 for ~5-6 reps. Grip is the limiter (left hand taps first) — that's deliberate, train the grip rather than bypass it. Set the DB down when grip gives.
**Grip is the ceiling on the pulling lifts, not the shoulder** — DB row, lat pulldown, and the push-day farmer carry all tap out at grip now. No straps.

**Face pull 47.5** — grip the rope ends in fists, knuckles up; that's what made 47.5 feel easy with the elbows still high. Keep the elbows-high / external-rotate cue; if 47.5 drops the elbows, go back to 45.
**Cable crunch 62.5 for form** — lighter on purpose, to get full ab flexion with the hips locked instead of yanking from the hip flexors. Earn the slow eccentric here before adding load back.
**Loads otherwise hold** — chest-supported row 40, pull-up bodyweight, lat pulldown dual-pulley 70, high cable curl 170, reverse fly 20.
**Shoulder management: ramp the tempo** — don't make every set all-slow-eccentric at once. The flares this cluster have been volume / time-under-tension, not weight.
**Left bicep first, every set** — keep the protocol as insurance even though the weak-left cleared.
**Pull-up frequency holds** — 4 sets here + 1 push warmup + 1-2 KB Tuesday. Slow tempo, not to failure.
**Cable lifts have per-equipment numbers** — pick what's free, log equipment + number.

exercises.notes: Scap activation. Squeeze the shoulder blades together, soft elbow.
Spine warm — slow, full ROM each direction.
Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — primes grip and the pulling chain before bar work.
Active hang, not collapsed — engage the lats, pull the shoulders DOWN away from the ears even at full extension.

sets.name: Behind-Back DB Shrug — Protective Activation (DO THIS FIRST)

exercises.equipment: DB pair, held behind the body
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40-50lb pair. 3 sets — first in the session.

**Why it's here, first:** this is the 'opposite movement' to all the pulling — a counter/decompression for the right shoulder. Front-loading it keeps pull day flare-free. It reads more like a stretch than a lift; that's the point.
- **DBs held BEHIND the body** at the sides of the hips/glutes — palms facing back
- **Shoulders pull DOWN and BACK** at the start — packed, not relaxed
- **Shrug UP and slightly BACK** — pinch the shoulder blades at the top
- **Hold 1s at the top**, slow descent
- **Pack DOWN, NOT up** as the resting position — the lower position IS the work
- Chest open, not slouched

sets.notes: Protective trap-chain activation, front of the session. ~4 min. Light-to-moderate, peak-squeeze — a decompression, not a max effort.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** Bodyweight. 4 sets of 6-8.
- **Straight bar** — the variant that's been feeling best
- **Active hang start**, not collapsed
- **Pull elbows DOWN to ribs**, NOT chin to bar
- **Chest leads to the bar at the top**, eyes ahead, head neutral
- **Slow eccentric ~2-3s**, active hang at the bottom of every rep — no dropping
- **Stop the set when the rep stops being clean** — never kip. The limiter now is strength + clean form, not the shoulder; quality reps, frequency over max effort.

sets.name: 🔆 DB Rack / Bench Block — Chest-Supported Row (Spotlight) + DB Row + Incline Curl + Reverse Fly (Spotlight) (3 Rounds)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40. 3 sets of 10-12.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the glued-chest row, drilled:**
- **Chest stays GLUED to the incline bench** the whole set — if the chest peels off to heave the DBs, the weight's ahead of the form
- **Pull the elbow toward the HIP, not the armpit** — keeps it in the lats
- **Don't rotate the torso** — both sides of the chest stay on the pad, no twisting up for the last reps
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the shoulder blade protract, then re-pull from the stretch
- **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze** at the top, no DB slam at the bottom

**Reflection:** does the chest stay glued and the torso stay square through the end of set 3, or does the chest start peeling to muscle the last reps? If it peels, that's the honest cap at 40 — slow the eccentric, don't heave.

**LOAD:** 70/80/90 ascending pyramid — one set per round (70, then 80, then 90). No straps.
- **Chest-supported on the incline bench** — same setup as the chest-supported row
- **Pull the elbow toward the HIP, not the armpit**
- **Don't rotate the torso** — chest glued, no twisting
- **Slow 2s descent, 1s squeeze** on the 70 and 80 sets — those hold clean form
- **On the 90 set, single-count tempo is honest** — grip won't hold a 2s eccentric there, so don't force it; drive the elbow, control what you can, and aim for ~5 clean reps before form breaks rather than grinding sloppy ones
- **Grip is the limiter** (left hand taps first) — set the DB down when grip gives, not when the back fails.

**LOAD:**
- **Incline bench, 25lb DBs** (default) — preacher-style chest-supported curl, 3 sets of 8-10
- **Actual preacher bench when it's open** — EZ bar, 2×10 on the bar felt clean; take the real preacher station whenever it's free, it locks the upper arm better than the incline lean

- **Incline bench ~45°, lean in chest-first** — armpit and the back of the upper arm flat on the pad; the upper arm stays flat the ENTIRE rep (don't lift the elbow)
- **Left arm first, every set** (DB version) — keep the protocol as insurance
- **Full stretch at the bottom — pause 2s**
- **Curl smoothly to the peak squeeze**, no swing; 2-3s eccentric
- **Both arms unsupported** (DB version) — keep both sides equal in quality, especially late in the block

**LOAD:** 20lb. 3 sets of 12 — cap at 12 with a slower eccentric rather than chasing reps.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the rear-delt sweep that protects the shoulder:**
- **30° reverse-incline** (chest-down on the incline bench), DBs hanging fully extended at the start
- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED throughout** — these are a sweep, NOT a row; the elbow angle never changes
- **Lead with the elbow, hand passive** — the hand never lifts first
- **Wings out and slightly UP to shoulder height** — sweep wide, don't lift, don't shrug
- **Hold the top a beat, then 2s eccentric** — control the drop, no swinging the DBs back up

**Reflection:** does the work stay in the rear delts / mid-traps with the elbow fixed and no shrug, or does it drift into the upper traps and momentum by rep 10? If it drifts, cap the set — strict 12 beats a swung 15. This is shoulder-health work; quality is the whole point.

sets.notes: One trip to the DB rack covers all 4 lifts. Incline bench at ~30° for the rows + reverse fly (30° reverse-incline), set to ~45° for the incline curl. 3 rounds.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD (pick whichever station's free, log which one):**
- **Dual pulley: 70** (the current home — 'very little pain' here)
- **Regular lat pulldown machine: 140**
- **Cable column: 52.5-57.5**
- **Cable pulley: 47.5**

3 sets.
- **Wide grip near the bend** — more lat isolation, less bicep
- **Slight backward lean ~15°, NO further** — more = it becomes a row
- **Pull the bar to the UPPER CHEST — NEVER behind the neck**
- **'Lats squeezing oranges into the back pockets'** at the bottom
- **1s pause at the contraction, 2s controlled return** to a full overhead stretch
- **Grip is the limiter at the end** — that's the honest cap, same as the DB row.

sets.name: Cable Column — Face Pull (3 Sets at 47.5)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** cable column 47.5.
- **Grip the rope ends in fists, knuckles up** — that's the change that made 47.5 feel easy with the elbows still high; keep it
- **Pull the rope to face level** — not to the chest
- **ELBOWS HIGH (above the shoulders)** — the make-or-break cue; this is what moves the work into the back
- **External-rotate at the top** — knuckles point UP, like the top of a double-biceps pose
- **1s peak hold**, then a slow 2s return — let the cable pull the arms back, don't drop
- Rear-delt + mid-trap + external-rotator health work — the right-shoulder-protective end of pull day
- **If the front of the shoulder takes over, the elbows have dropped** — re-set them high. If 47.5 drops the elbows, go back to 45.

sets.name: Cable Column Finisher — High Cable Curl + Cable Crunch (2-3 Sets)

exercises.equipment: cable column (low pulley, single D-handle, one arm at a time)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD (single arm — scales differ, log which station):**
- Cable column (single D-handle): 170
- Pulley / weight-stack station: ~120
2 working sets per arm.
- **Single arm at a time, one D-handle** — stand sideways, arm out at shoulder level
- **Upper arm parallel to the floor, FIXED** — the whole point of the high-cable variant
- **Curl the hand toward the ear**, peak squeeze
- **Left arm first**; slow eccentric, no bounce at the start

**LOAD (pick whichever station's free, log which one):**
- **Cable pulley (rope): 62.5** — lighter on purpose, the form-first number
- **Cable column (rope): scale down similarly for form**

3 sets.
- **Lighter load = real ab flexion.** 77.5 was heavy enough to turn it into a hip-flexor yank; 62.5 lets the spine actually round and the slow eccentric come back. Earn the form here before adding load.
- **Kneel under the high cable**
- **HIPS LOCKED** — the most important cue. The hips do not move.
- **Crunch from the abs ONLY** — the spine flexes, the hips stay put. Hips moving = hip-flexor work, not abs.
- **Chest toward the thighs**, hold the crunch 1 second
- **Slow eccentric, all the way** — at 62.5 the controlled drop IS available; use it, that's the whole reason for the lighter load.

sets.notes: Same cable column as the face pull. 2 rounds = 2 sets each; round the cable crunch to 3 if there's time and the abs aren't fried.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block (Permanent Every-Gym-Day Closing Block)

exercises.notes: 30s each arm at MID elbow position. Pec minor lengthen.
Passive hang. Don't engage — let the shoulders unpack and the spine decompress.
30s each side. Draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.

sets.notes: 5 minutes of recovery work, non-negotiable closing block.

tips: **Behind-back shrug stays FIRST** — protective decompression that keeps pull day flare-free. It can't be the piece a rushed session drops.
**DB row holds 70/80/90, no straps.** Top set is 90 for ~5-6 reps. Grip is the limiter (left hand) and that's deliberate — train it, don't bypass it.
**Spotlight: chest-supported row + reverse fly.** Row drills the glued-chest, elbow-to-hip pattern at 40; reverse fly drills the fixed-elbow rear-delt sweep at 20, capped by tempo.
**Face pull 47.5** — grip the rope ends in fists, knuckles up; that's what unlocked it. Keep the elbows high; drop to 45 if the elbows fall.
**Cable crunch 62.5 — form-first.** Lighter to win back true ab flexion (hips locked, slow eccentric) instead of a hip-flexor yank. Earn the form before adding load.
**Grip is the ceiling on pulling, not the shoulder** — DB row, lat pulldown, farmer carry all tap out at grip now. No straps.
**Loads otherwise hold** — pull-up bodyweight, lat pulldown dual-pulley 70, high cable curl 170.
**Shoulder management: ramp the tempo** — don't make every set all-slow-eccentric at once.
**Left bicep first, every set** — keep the protocol as insurance.
**Cable lifts list per-equipment numbers** — lat pulldown (70 dual pulley / 140 machine / 52.5-57.5 column / 47.5 pulley). Pick what's free, log it.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, permanent every gym day.**
Rest: shrug 60s, 2.5 min pull-ups, 90s DB block, 2 min lat pulldown, 90s face pull, 60s finisher.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state pull week with the protective shrug leading. The spotlights drill the two lifts that keep the shoulder healthy — the chest-supported row's glued-chest pattern and the reverse fly's fixed-elbow rear-delt sweep — because clean upper-back and rear-delt work is the counterweight to all the pressing. The DB row holds its heavy top set with grip, not straps, as the honest cap. Building decades, not weeks.
